key_highlights: ASX shed $90b in a week amid rate-rise fears and oil price surge, though index edged higher on the day with Fed meeting in focus
Iron ore crash confirmed, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX and broader materials sector
ANZ.AX completes 3,500-job cut programme; restructuring plan still faces long execution path
Major private hospital operator to be broken up after lenders back consortium bid, reshaping ASX healthcare landscape
Australian fuel prices set to rise 30c/litre on global oil spike, pressuring Qantas.AX and consumer spending
Housing market shows no spring bounce; auction volumes weak, house prices under downward pressure
Mining cap-raise activity surges as Canaccord leads dash for cash; small-caps PolarX, Sunstone Metals, Manuka Resources in focus
Immigration policy overhaul debate intensifies, threatening labour supply for agriculture and construction sectors
Santos.SAN preservation deemed a national sacrifice, with energy security implications for Australia

sectors.trend: Iron ore crash confirmed; commodity price weakness pressures major miners. Small-cap gold and critical-mines names (PLC Resources, PolarX, Sunstone Metals, Manuka Resources) attract speculative flows. Canaccord-led cap raises signal capital-raising stress across junior miners.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression. Gold miners (NVA.AX, GWN.AX) may benefit from safe-haven rotation. Junior miners face dilution risk from cap raises.

sectors.trend: ANZ.AX post-3,500-job cut restructuring underway but execution risk remains. Private hospital operator breakup signals credit stress in healthcare lending. Rate-rise fears weigh on bank valuations and NIM outlook.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate uncertainty. Hospital operator breakup may create M&A opportunities for IAG.AX-linked health insurers.

sectors.trend: Oil spike drives 30c fuel price rise, squeezing airlines and transport. Santos.SAN preservation reflects national energy-security priority but at economic cost. NuScale Power 15% jump signals nuclear renaissance theme.
sectors.implications: Qantas.AX, SYD.AX face cost inflation. Woodside.AX, Santos.SAN benefit from energy-security narrative. Nuclear/uranium names (LNG.AX, SMR.AX) see thematic tailwind.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator breakup after lender-backed consortium bid signals sector consolidation. CSL.AX remains defensive anchor.
sectors.implications: Consolidation may benefit larger operators (AHC.AX, IAG.AX health arm). CSL.AX offers defensive stability amid volatility.

sectors.trend: No spring bounce in auction market; house prices under pressure. Jewelry chain closes 53 stores. Lululemon guidance downgrade signals global consumer softness. Young homeowners welcome falling prices but wealth effect is negative.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure. WES.AX, WBC.AX consumer lending at risk. Property developers under stress.

sectors.trend: AI theme dominant globally: Foxconn bullish signal for Nvidia, Oracle $664B backlog, Anthropic IPO, Wiley AI monetisation. Trump vs tech chiefs on AI pace. Musk robot economy messaging.
sectors.implications: ASX tech exposure limited but CSL.AX (biotech-AI), WES.AX (fintech) benefit. Global AI capex cycle supports hardware/semiconductor supply chains.

Rate-rise fears and Fed meeting as near-term volatility driver

Superannuation system reform debate as medium-term policy risk

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into gold (NVA.AX) and critical minerals (LNG.AX)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate rise / Fed hawkish surprise
risk_assessment.mitigation: Shorten duration in fixed income; favour dividend-paying defensives (CSL.AX, WES.AX)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Oil price spike and fuel cost inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight Qantas.AX, SYD.AX; favour energy producers (WDS.AX, STOL.AX)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Immigration policy disruption to labour supply
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor construction and agriculture sector earnings; favour automation/tech beneficiaries
Reduce REIT and property developer exposure; monitor bank NPL trends

opportunities.rationale: Iron ore crash diverts capital to gold (safe haven) and strategic minerals with government support

opportunities.rationale: Rate uncertainty and $90b ASX drawdown favour income-stable names

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce or hedge iron ore exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Confirmed iron ore crash threatens BHP/RIO/FMG earnings through FY27

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight airlines and transport on fuel cost spike
defensive_moves.rationale: 30c fuel rise compresses margins; staff shortages add operational risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim REIT and property developer exposure

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid junior miners with pending cap raises
defensive_moves.rationale: Canaccord-led mining cap-raise wave signals dilution risk and weak capital markets

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile and under pressure over 1–3 months. Fed meeting outcome, iron ore price trajectory, and oil spike are dominant drivers. $90b weekly drawdown suggests further downside risk unless commodity prices stabilise. Rate-rise fears cap upside for rate-sensitive sectors.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious. Immigration policy overhaul may constrain GDP growth and labour supply. Housing correction and superannuation reform debate add structural uncertainty. However, energy-security policy, AI capex cycle, and critical-minerals investment provide offsetting positives. ASX likely to trade in a range pending policy clarity.
